citations.narrative:
The facility is not adequately cleaning the animal enclosures. There were 5 primary enclosures housing 6 striped skunks
that have excessive feces soiling the floor and the bedding for the animals. The enclosures have solid flooring that has
feces or a thin layer of moist organic material encompassing most of the floor space. The various types of bedding that
are provided appear moist and soiled with urine and fecal material causing them to be discolored with a yellow/brown
appearance. There are large piles of fecal material in the corners of some of the enclosures that have been pressed down
into the flooring by the animals walking through the area. In one enclosure there is a large pool of thick brown liquid that
appears to be due to water being splashed from the water receptacle and mixing with the fecal material. In two of the
enclosures the piles of feces have attracted flies which are flying near and inside of the enclosures, and maggots could be
observed crawling through the piles of feces. The skunks must walk through feces or over soiled bedding material to
reach their food and water receptacles. Additionally, the metal wiring of the enclosures appears to contain cobwebs and
fur stuck to the walls and ceiling of the enclosures.
Accumulations of feces, urine, and soiled bedding are harmful to the animals as they can spread disease, attract pests,
and cause unpleasant odors. Excreta shall be removed from primary enclosures as often as necessary to prevent
contamination of the animals contained therein and to minimize disease hazards and to reduce odors.
Correct by 12:00 pm on 22-September-2026
A complete routine inspection was conducted starting on 21-September-2026. This inspection report is limited to the
Direct non-compliance identified during that inspection. An additional inspection report will be delivered with the other
issues identified during this inspection.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
